Lessons.Title: Solve Problems With Equal Groups
ExplanationParagraphs: Original warm-up Estimation Exploration asks for 'too low', 'about right' and 'too high' estimates for4×18, not one universally correct set. Actual exact product4×18=72, useful estimate benchmark4×20=80. Teachers judge estimate explanations.

Activity1 original farmers market problem1: a seller has SEVEN DOZEN eggs at closing. Original cartoon photo checked: a carton has2×6=12 eggs; one dozen=12, so7×12=84 eggs. First-party grouping7×(10+2)=70+14=84.

Activity1 original problem2: five rows of 15 chairs for a music performance, total5×15=75 chairs; group as5×(10+5)=50+25=75. Partners make a poster showing their chosen representation, then gallery-walk those posters in Activity2.
Activity1 original problem3: tabletop side lengths4 feet and16 feet, area4×16=64 SQUARE FEET (not 64 feet or perimeter40 feet). Draw4 rows of16 unit square areas or decompose16=10+6.

Activity2 Gallery Walk: Problems with Teen Numbers is an actual partner walk between original learner-produced posters, comparing and connecting different chair models. MLR7 Compare and Connect emphasizes why multiple models yield the same75 chairs. Student-generated poster, oral explanation and group reflection are not scalar-graded.

Use equal groups, counting, grids, cubes, distributive property and place-value decomposition to multiply within100 with teen factors. The publisher Bags of Oranges Cool-down is teacher-gated, source PDF and image art are not copied; tests and Stage D unrun.

KeyConcepts.Title: Teen factor decomposition
KeyConcepts.Definition: Split a teen number into ten and ones to ease multiplication.

KeyConcepts.Title: Area units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Area is product of two linear side lengths, with squared units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Estimates
KeyConcepts.Definition: Estimation can have many justified too-low or too-high values.
